approach: schema-driven code generation for two-process shared-memory passthrough bridges, with stub processes and a round-trip check against existing SkyCraft-family headers
scope_note: a scaffold, not a playable mashup: it does not run or patch games, does not ship a host-side plugin, and its README states it has no on-hardware verification.

description: Both games run at once: Saints Row owns the world, vehicles and camera, while on foot Minecraft moves the player, renders from SR3's camera and is depth-tested against SR3's depth buffer. Raycasts turn SR3's floors and walls into invisible Minecraft collision, Minecraft swords, arrows and mobs damage SR3's people through stand-ins, and Minecraft TNT becomes Saints Row explosions. The README calls it early and only partly verified in the real game.
creator: SawyerTheNerd
requirements: Windows 10/11 and Saints Row: The Third Remastered on Steam; building from source needs Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools, CMake, Python 3.10+ with several packages and a portable JDK 25. The first Minecraft start downloads Minecraft 26.3; no binary release is published.
approach: dinput8.dll link in SR3 + Minecraft Fabric mod over WebSocket and shared memory, with a Present-hook compositor (derived from universal-modder's Minecraft x GTA V example)
ai_assistance: The README credits say it was written with Claude Code (Anthropic), including the reverse engineering notes.
review_note: The GitHub README, MIT LICENSE and file tree were reviewed on 2026-10-08 (single push 2026-10-05, no releases). No independent catalogue play-test was performed.

name: Ultrakill64
summary: A proof-of-concept that drops Super Mario 64's Mario into ULTRAKILL's sandbox using libsm64.
description: A BepInEx plugin that uses the libsm64 Unity runtime to put Super Mario 64's Mario, with his original movement code, into ULTRAKILL. The creator describes it as a few hours' proof of concept that barely works outside the sandbox and has issues far from the origin or with heavy geometry.
creator: Squaresweets
requirements: ULTRAKILL with BepInEx; the prebuilt Ultrakill64.dll and sm64bundle from the repository's Build folder; the user's own Super Mario 64 (US) ROM named baserom.us.z64 next to the game executable; played in the sandbox's clash mode.
approach: BepInEx plugin using libsm64-unity
notes: Same creator as UltraDoom and Ultrakill-in-Ultrakill.
review_note: The GitHub README and file tree were reviewed on 2026-10-08 (prebuilt DLL in the Build folder, no licence file, no tagged releases). No independent catalogue play-test or binary safety review was performed.

name: Ultrakill in Ultrakill
summary: Plays ULTRAKILL on in-game terminals inside ULTRAKILL, three instances deep.
description: Three ULTRAKILL instances run at once; each frame, screenshots are passed between them through memory-mapped files and drawn on in-game terminals, and dedicated keys switch which instance the player controls, giving a game-inside-a-game-inside-a-game.
creator: Squaresweets
requirements: ULTRAKILL with BepInEx, and three separate copies of the game folder each running the plugin (the prebuilt UltrakillInUltrakill.dll is in the repository).
approach: BepInEx plugin; three game instances exchange frames through memory-mapped files
review_note: The GitHub README and file tree were reviewed on 2026-10-08 (prebuilt DLL and plugin source, no licence file, no tagged releases). No independent catalogue play-test or binary safety review was performed.

summary: Lets you play Tomb Raider 1 as Super Mario 64's Mario, switching between Mario and Lara.

name: MinecraftNES
summary: A NES emulator built entirely from vanilla Minecraft resource-pack shaders.
description: Emulates the NES inside unmodified Minecraft Java 1.16 using only resource-pack shader programs, with the ROM converted into a texture. It supports mapper 0 and mapper 2 games and includes a TAS input mode.
creator: Suso (5uso)
requirements: Minecraft Java 1.16.x with Fabulous graphics, and a mapper 0 or mapper 2 NES ROM converted with the repository's ROM.py into the pack's ROM texture.

name: Retromod 2.0 (and GNES / GEMU) — ckosmic's Garry's Mod emulators
summary: A lineage of in-game console emulators for Garry's Mod, from GNES (2016) to the RetroArch-based Retromod 2.0.
description: ckosmic built a series of Garry's Mod addons for playing retro console games on in-game screens: GNES (2016), which ran the JSNES emulator and was billed as the first gaming-system emulator in Garry's Mod; GEMU (2017), a multi-system emulator for NES, SNES, Game Boy, GBA and Genesis; the original Retromod (2018); and Retromod 2.0 (2021), which uses RetroArch as its backend. Retromod 2.0 is the current addon; the earlier ones are kept as history.
guest: NES, SNES, Game Boy / GBC / GBA, Sega Genesis and other RetroArch-supported systems
creator: ckosmic
requirements: Garry's Mod on Windows; Retromod 2.0 uses RetroArch as its backend and needs the user's own ROMs (see its Workshop installation instructions).
approach: Garry's Mod addons rendering emulators (JSNES, then RetroArch) onto in-game screen entities
notes: Same creator as G64. ckosmic's 2017 GEMU is unrelated to Nighthawk42's 2026 GEMU addon, which is catalogued separately. A Workshop comment suggests GNES may no longer work in current Garry's Mod.
review_note: The Steam Web API details and descriptions of Workshop items 736083419 (GNES), 945777403 (GEMU), 1457560331 (Retromod, deprecated) and 2438477032 (Retromod 2.0) were reviewed on 2026-10-09; all are public, not banned and owned by the same creator account as G64. No independent catalogue play-test was performed.

name: Ultracraft
summary: Plays the real ULTRAKILL inside real Minecraft: Java Edition, drawing it into Minecraft's window.
description: A Fabric mod plus a BepInEx plugin (UltraBridge) that runs ULTRAKILL alongside Minecraft 1.21.11 and draws it into Minecraft's window. Minecraft's blocks and mobs become ULTRAKILL's world and enemies; the README documents bosses, layer-themed arenas, the shop and upgrades, Cyber Grind, fight music, cheats and LAN co-op.

name: MGBridge (Minecraft and Garry's Mod)
summary: Historical bridge that lets friends play Minecraft and Garry's Mod at the same time in a linked room.

name: FortressCraft (FortCraft)
summary: Plays Minecraft as a Team Fortress 2 mercenary, with TF2's classes, weapons and buildings running against Minecraft's world and mobs.
description: A two-process passthrough in which Minecraft draws the world and owns its blocks, mobs, dimensions and saves, while a locally built Team Fortress 2 bridge supplies the player, classes, weapons, projectiles, Engineer buildings, menus and HUD. The creator documents mob targeting, block breaking and explosions, and lists known gaps such as Medic healing against Minecraft mobs. It is a source preview built from the Source SDK, not a one-click installer.
creator: VVRLD
requirements: Windows 11, Team Fortress 2 and Source SDK Base 2013 Multiplayer on Steam, Minecraft Java Edition, Git, JDK 25 and Visual Studio with C++/MSBuild. The user clones Valve's Source SDK 2013 and applies the repository's patch; the Fabric side targets Minecraft 26.3 with Fabric Loader 0.19.5. Single-player/LAN only; no game files are included.
approach: Minecraft Fabric mod + Source SDK 2013 TF2 bridge exchanging state over a shared-memory protocol
ai_assistance: The repository description says it was made using Claude and ChatGPT.
review_note: The GitHub README, MIT LICENSE and repository metadata (created and pushed 2026-10-06, no releases) were reviewed on 2026-10-09; the creator calls it an experimental source preview that is not clean-machine tested. No independent catalogue play-test was performed.
